title: Producer/consumer with a bounded queue.Queue (no threads)
problem_md:
Before wiring threads, model the scheduling deterministically. Several producers (report downloaders) push items into a **bounded** `queue.Queue(maxsize)`; one consumer (DB writer) drains it in batches.

```python
def simulate(producers: list[list[str]], maxsize: int, batch: int) -> dict
```

Run in *ticks* until every producer is empty **and** the queue is empty. In each tick:
1. Each producer, in list order, tries `put_nowait` of its **next** item. On `queue.Full` the item stays with the producer (it retries next tick) and you count one `full_events`.
2. The consumer takes up to `batch` items with `get_nowait` (stop early on `queue.Empty`), appending each to `processed`.

Return `{"processed": [...], "full_events": int, "ticks": int}`. Raise `ValueError` if `maxsize < 1` or `batch < 1` (note `Queue(0)` would mean *unbounded*).

examples.explanation: Tick 1: a1 queued, b1 hits Full, consumer takes a1. Tick 2: a2 queued, b1 Full again, consumer takes a2. Tick 3: b1 queued and consumed.

hints: Keep each producer's remaining items in a `collections.deque`; only `popleft()` after `put_nowait` succeeds.
Loop condition: `while any(pending) or not q.empty():` - increment `ticks` at the start of each iteration.
solution_md:
The bound is the point: with `maxsize`, a fast producer can't buffer an entire report in memory - it gets `queue.Full` (or, with blocking `put()`, waits). That is **backpressure**. `queue.Queue` is FIFO and thread-safe (internally a `deque` + `threading.Condition`), so this exact logic carries over to threads: producers call blocking `q.put(item)`, the consumer loops `q.get()` / `q.task_done()`, and shutdown uses a sentinel per consumer or `q.join()`. (Python 3.13 adds `Queue.shutdown()`.)

`try/except queue.Full ... else: popleft()` only removes an item after it was actually queued - no lost items. Work is O(total items x ticks-per-item). The same model applies to SQS/Celery: bounded in-flight work, consumer batch size, and retry of rejected puts.
